eval.title: CVS Health Stock Looks Like A Buy - My Added Value

call.headline_quote: so then you know okay I might start accumulating and have a good return over the next three to 5 years if I am patient and I know what I own

base_metric.name: eps
base_metric.quote: still targeting that $7 per year earnings per share down from 860

reasons.claim: The P/E is a third of the average S&P 500 company, giving a margin of safety on a stock that has fallen over 50%.
reasons.quote: the p ratio is a third of the average sap 5 00 company

data_check.gap_note: he says 0.33, as-of 8.6507 (FY2023); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: Insurance underwriting is cyclical and in aggregate has worked out well over time even though it swings between good and bad years, so the current downturn should eventually reverse.
reasons.quote: in aggregate the insurance business has worked out very well but it hasn't been a oneway street

reasons.claim: Management bought back stock when it was expensive and has now halted buybacks after the price collapsed, which he calls insanely stupid capital allocation.
reasons.quote: we do not expect to repurchase any additional shares for the remainder of 2024

data_check.gap_note: trajectory visible at T0; no number stated

reasons.claim: Regulatory rate-setting under the Affordable Care framework is insufficient relative to costs, creating a structural long-term risk for the insurance business.
reasons.quote: the rate is insufficient which means that there will be some ups and downs with the health the insurance and that is the key long-term structural risk for CVS Health going forward

reasons.claim: Government involvement and regulatory headwinds in US healthcare are a reason he personally stays away from healthcare insurance investments.
reasons.quote: regulatory headwinds which is a reason why I'm not going to healthcare insurance into the US

external_facts_used: Analyst models still projecting EPS of $9 for 2026
UBS cut CVS to neutral after earnings miss and slashed its price target
$900 million medical cost overrun split into $500 million seasonal and $400 million utilization-driven factors
CEO commentary on receiving an insufficient final rate notice from regulators
Reference to Warren Buffett's 1977 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter on insurance underwriting cycles

critic.notes: He frames CVS as cheap with a margin of safety and a possible accumulate for patient investors, but explicitly says he personally won't invest in US healthcare insurance due to regulatory risk; that reads as fair_hold, not relative_buy.
